newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dollar, RBI inactive.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dollar, RBI inactive.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.8750/8850 against the dollar on Tuesday, little changed from the day's opening level, dealers said.
Dollar saw some gains during the day on the back of some large dollar demand before the rupee recovered, dealers said.
"There were some deals at 35.8950 - the highest level the dollar touched," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
A Calcutta-based bank was in the market and bought dollars upto 35.8850 level, dealers said.
"From here (we) expect the dollar to gradually move higher towards 35.90 and beyond as we move nearer to the budget and the usual month-end demand," said a foreign bank in a report.
Contrary to expectations, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was not active on Tuesday, dealers said.
"They didn't hit any bank, but I believe they did swaps with those who went to them," said a dealer at a leading bank, referring to RBI's dollar purchases in the swap market.

"The market was caught on the wrong foot on Friday when the RBI made its appearance (in the swap market), forced by underestimation of the India Development Bond (IDB) redemption in foreign currency," said a dealer at a major bank.
Dealers expect the IDB redemption, due later this week, to see an outflow of almost $1.0 billion in foreign exchange.
The RBI bought over $75 million in major swap deals on Friday.

In the absence of RBI's active intervention, the forward dollar premia rose after opening lower. August dollars closed at 1.31/1.33 rupees compared with the opening .129/1.32 rupees. The six month annualised premium ended at 6.69 percent compared with last week's closing rate of 6.91 percent, dealers said.
Some dealers said RBI also bought spot dollars, at levels higher than its previous purchases, but other dealers said they could not confirm purchases in the spot market on Tuesday.
